tasks.short: Direct vessel course and speed using local knowledge

steps.what: Review local winds, weather, depths, tides, currents and hazards for the vessel's present situation
Determine the appropriate course and speed for the current conditions
Direct the bridge team on course and speed and verify the vessel's response
outputs: course and speed directed under current conditions

tasks.design: Retain local-condition assessment and course/speed direction with the captain or pilot using {OPS_SYSTEM}, the existing bridge navigation equipment. Integrated navigation aids support the work, but their existing calculations do not establish less required attention or direction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe directions depend on local and changing conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing navigation equipment already assists the task; no additional labour-saving mechanism is established.
tasks.still_hard: Reconcile local observations, traffic and vessel response.
tasks.human_edge: Apply local knowledge and direct the bridge team.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bridge navigation aids assist course and speed decisions while captains and pilots retain local-condition judgement.

assumptions: Boundary includes consulting conditions, deciding and communicating directions, not separate statutory logkeeping. No record-writing or report deliverable is hidden in a live step; this statement asks for vessel direction.

Existing chart/weather/instrument producers supply position, time, depth, tide/current and weather information with source and currency. Missing or doubtful information requires normal human verification. No new sensor, feed or unpriced capture is assumed.

Native integrated displays and existing control assistance are considered first. Lookup and interpretation remain explicit in s1; no invented chart-hunting or repeated copying baseline supports reducing them. OTHER means the physical bridge.
Provisional B=100, R=100, gross=0; incremental=0; net=0. Shares are independent of means priors. No automatic message or control commit is proposed.
unknowns: Required watch and pilot duties with existing navigation aids
research_questions: Observe direction work separately from existing navigation-system runtime.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Existing aids are already in the baseline; no mechanism reduces local assessment, decisions or live directions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe the vessel, traffic and crew activities for unsafe operations
inputs: existing navigation indications and traffic picture

steps.what: Judge the unsafe condition and determine the required intervention
Intervene with the crew to prevent unsafe operations and verify that the condition is corrected
inputs: crew response and actual vessel conditions
outputs: unsafe operation prevented or further intervention required

tasks.design: Keep active safety supervision and intervention with the captain or pilot at {OTHER}, the vessel bridge and work areas. Existing {OPS_SYSTEM} warnings can assist detection, but do not replace observing crew activity or verifying a safe response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unsafe operations can involve behavior and circumstances outside instrument signals.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing alarms assist supervision without establishing a lower human duty.
tasks.still_hard: Recognize a developing unsafe situation and secure an effective response.
tasks.human_edge: Intervene with operational authority and verify the outcome.

ambition.what: Preserve active prevention of unsafe operations.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: equipment warnings do not cover all unsafe vessel and crew operations.

assumptions: Boundary is active prevention, including live directions and verification. A later incident report, if needed, is distinct; no report or record write appears in this statement or is folded into observation.
Existing instruments and direct observation provide actual states, timestamps and activity. No new behavior classification, automated enforcement or extra crew data entry is proposed.
Native warning features are considered. Their existing runtime is not focal labour, and an additional screen or template does not reduce the observation, decision or intervention.
Provisional B=100, R=100, gross=0; incremental=0; net=0, independent of means priors. All communications are direct human intervention, with no automated send or commit.
unknowns: Whether existing warnings change any required supervision duty
research_questions: Observe unsafe-operation prevention and determine which conditions instruments cannot establish.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No concrete change reduces the required active supervision and intervention.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Serve as docking master at port or berth

steps.what: Review the assigned berth, vessel characteristics and current port conditions
inputs: existing berth assignment and port information

steps.what: Agree the docking approach and responsibilities with bridge, tug and berth personnel
inputs: tug and berth personnel's current readiness

steps.what: Direct the vessel's docking manoeuvre while observing clearances and vessel response
inputs: actual clearances, movement and environmental conditions
outputs: vessel positioned at berth under docking direction

steps.what: Confirm the vessel's final berth position and completion of the docking handover
inputs: vessel positioned at berth under docking direction
outputs: docking completion confirmed with berth team

tasks.design: Retain docking-master preparation, coordination and live manoeuvre direction using existing {OPS_SYSTEM} navigation aids and {TELEPHONY} radio communications. A planning display does not replace clearance observation, live instructions or confirmation with the berth team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Docking depends on changing local conditions and coordinated physical actions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing aids support the task; no additional software-only labour reduction is established.
tasks.still_hard: Judge clearances and vessel response while coordinating several parties.
tasks.human_edge: Direct the manoeuvre and establish mutual understanding.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: docking-master work requires real-time coordination and observation of vessel response.

assumptions: Boundary includes berth-reference review, planning dialogue, manoeuvre direction and docking handover. Separate voyage/port logkeeping is not hidden within those actions; no written-report deliverable is stated here.

Existing port personnel supply berth assignment and current readiness; instruments and direct observation supply actual vessel movement and conditions. s2/s4 count obtaining current confirmations, not assuming planned readiness is actual readiness.

Native navigation and berth information are considered first. No avoidable re-entry or invented search baseline is assumed; automated movement or tug instructions are not introduced. OTHER means the physical bridge and berth view.
Provisional B=100, R=100, gross=0; incremental=0; net=0, independent of means priors. Radio exchanges are direct human conversation, not machine sends.
unknowns: Required docking-master presence with existing aids
research_questions: Observe docking preparation, live direction and handover separately.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The sequence explicitly retains reference review and communications; no concrete mechanism shortens required docking work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult navigation sources to determine and direct ship movements

steps.what: Consult maps, charts, weather reports and navigation equipment for the current passage
inputs: existing current charts and weather reports
outputs: reviewed navigation source information and uncertainties

steps.what: Determine ship movements by reconciling the sources with current conditions
inputs: reviewed navigation source information and uncertainties

steps.what: Direct the bridge team on the determined ship movements and confirm understanding
outputs: ship movements directed with bridge-team understanding

tasks.design: Use existing {OPS_SYSTEM} charts, weather displays and navigation instruments for explicit source consultation. The captain or pilot reconciles uncertainties and directs the bridge team; an additional aggregation view is not credited with reducing required source checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources can disagree or become stale during a passage.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing integrated navigation equipment already presents the core information.
tasks.still_hard: Recognize source limitations and determine appropriate movement.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret sources in actual navigational context.

ambition.what: Maintain careful source consultation and accountable movement decisions.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: navigation equipment can combine source information while navigators retain source verification and movement judgement.

assumptions: Boundary explicitly separates consulting sources, determining movement and communicating directions. It does not contain an unstated report or record write; separate logkeeping remains a distinct task.

Existing chart/weather producers supply edition, validity, location coverage and provenance; instruments supply actual readings and timestamps. Missing or contradictory information requires normal verification in s1/s2. No new feed or unpriced tagging is assumed.
Native source views are considered first. No invented paper-chart or manual-copying baseline supports a saving, and current equipment runtime is not human labour. OTHER is the physical bridge.
Provisional B=100, R=100, gross=0; incremental=0; net=0, independent of means priors. No autonomous direction or machine send is introduced.
unknowns: Whether existing source presentation leaves any avoidable handling beyond required checks
research_questions: Measure source consultation separately from system computation and movement judgement.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Required source consultation and directions remain explicit; existing integration alone establishes no incremental labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Captains, mates and pilots retain navigational judgement, supervision and docking direction with existing bridge aids.
reach: Port and tug personnel: coordinate actual readiness
skills_to_grow: Separate aid runtime from human watch duties
role.ambitious_version: A vessel navigator who uses existing aids critically and retains responsibility for movements, crew coordination and local conditions.
